# Keyword Optimizer — Peer Handoff & Mutation Sensitivity

This optimizer mutates the live account (pause, match-type swap, cross-negatives, duplicate resolution, zombie cleanup, optionally bid-strategy targets via KW-E08). Before generating any operations, it must consult fresh peer audits and recent peer mutations.

Two distinct mechanisms:

1. **Peer Audit Freshness Table** — fresh peer audit reports that gate or contextualize mutations.
2. **Mutation Sensitivity Matrix** — recent peer *mutations* in `context/account-changelog.md` that compound risk if stacked.

Both are consulted in **Phase 0.4: Peer Pre-flight** of `SKILL.md`.

---

## Peer Audit Freshness Table

`/keyword-auditor` is excluded — it is the upstream auditor for this optimizer and is consumed via `context/analysis/keyword-audit.md` in Phase 0.1. Its slot in the 10-peer table is filled by `/account-auditor`.

| Peer skill | Report file | Fresh window | Layer | Verdict if dirty/critical |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/quality-score-auditor` | `context/analysis/quality-score-audit.md` | ≤ 7 days | Eff | soft-warn |
| `/search-term-auditor` | `context/analysis/search-term-audit.md` | ≤ 7 days | Eff | soft-warn |
| `/budget-auditor` | `context/analysis/budget-audit.md` | ≤ 7 days | Bud | soft-warn |
| `/bidding-auditor` | `context/analysis/bidding-audit.md` | ≤ 7 days | Bid | soft-warn |
| `/competitive-analyst` | `context/analysis/competitive-audit.md` | ≤ 14 days | Comp | informational |
| `/lp-auditor` | `context/analysis/lp-audit.md` | ≤ 14 days | Conv | soft-warn |
| `/offer-auditor` | `context/analysis/offer-audit.md` | ≤ 30 days | Conv | soft-warn |
| `/tracking-specialist` | `context/analysis/tracking-audit.md` | ≤ 30 days | **M** | **HARD-BLOCK** if fail/critical |
| `/strategy-specialist` | `context/analysis/strategy-audit.md` | ≤ 30 days | **B** | **HARD-BLOCK** if unit economics missing/placeholder |
| `/account-auditor` | `context/analysis/account-audit.md` | ≤ 30 days | Struct | informational |

### Hard-block rule (universal)

If `/tracking-specialist` is fresh and reports failing/critical findings on a campaign in the operations plan, OR `/strategy-specialist` is fresh and unit economics are missing/placeholder — **refuse all mutations**. Print the failing finding(s) and the handoff command. Bid-strategy actions (KW-E08) are particularly sensitive to a missing `max_profitable_cpa` / `min_profitable_roas`; the existing Phase 0.3 already routes E08 to `/strategy-specialist` when those are absent — Phase 0.4 generalizes that gate to *all* mutation types.

**Hard-block is on the M / B layer being dirty**, not on the report being absent. Missing M/B reports degrade to soft-warn ("no fresh /tracking-specialist") — never auto-trigger a peer skill.

### Soft-warn rule

A fresh peer at Eff/Conv/Bud/Bid/Comp/Struct layers that flags issues on a campaign or ad group in the operations plan → surface in the dry-run "Cross-skill context" section, but do not block. Quote 1–3 findings (peer score, headline, date, affected campaign/ad-group when known).

Example surfaces:

- Fresh `/quality-score-auditor` shows QS 4 on an ad group containing keywords queued for KW-E03 match-type swap → soft-warn ("the swap may further hurt QS until ads relearn").
- Fresh `/search-term-auditor` shows uncovered n-gram waste on a campaign queued for KW-E01 pauses → soft-warn (consider negatives first, since pausing keywords doesn't stop the n-gram from triggering on broader matches elsewhere).
- Fresh `/budget-auditor` shows the campaign is budget-limited → soft-warn (pausing keywords here will redistribute spend, not save it).
- Fresh `/lp-auditor` shows LP failures on the campaign queued for cross-negatives (KW-E05) → soft-warn (the cannibalization may be a symptom of LP/offer mismatch, not keyword overlap).

### No fresh peer report

Never auto-trigger a peer skill from inside the optimizer. Note "no fresh {peer}" in the dry-run "Cross-skill context" so the operator knows the picture is incomplete and can run the peer themselves before approving.

### Freshness rule

The report header date inside the markdown is **canonical**. File mtime is a sanity check — if mtime is older than the header date by >3 days, treat the report as suspicious and surface the contradiction in the dry-run output (e.g. "tracking-audit.md header says 2026-04-15 but file mtime is 2026-04-08 — header date wins, but flag for operator review"). Never auto-defer to one or auto-override.

---

## Mutation Sensitivity Matrix

Read `context/account-changelog.md` (recommend ≤24h old; auto-refresh via `/account-changelog` if stale, or note the gap in dry-run if refresh declined). For every campaign and ad group in the operations plan, scan changelog entries within the windows below. Verdicts:

- **hard-block** — refuse mutation; require operator to remove the affected scope from the plan or pass an explicit override.
- **hard-warn** — list in dry-run "Cross-skill context" with a `WARN:` prefix; require operator to type "confirm" before proceeding to live apply.
- **soft-warn** — list in dry-run "Cross-skill context" as informational.

| Peer skill / source | Mutation type | Window | Scope match | Verdict | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/rsa-maker`, manual ad edits | new ad / RSA edit / pause | ≤ 7d | overlapping ad group | soft-warn | Mid-test ad rotation — pausing/swapping keywords now muddies the ad-level read |
| `/bidding-optimizer` | bid strategy or target adjustment | 2–7d | overlapping campaign | soft-warn | Bid math still resettling; keyword pauses change the volume signal smart bidding learns from |
| `/search-term-optimizer` | negatives added / search terms promoted | ≤ 7d | overlapping campaign or ad group | soft-warn | Cohort already shifting; stacking keyword pauses muddies which lever moved efficiency |
| `/account-auditor`, `/account-changelog` | campaign restructure (rebuild, merge, split, ad-group reorg) | ≤ 14d | overlapping campaign | hard-warn | Data discontinuity — keyword history pre-rebuild is not comparable; pause/match-swap decisions on stale tier data are unsafe |
| `/keyword-optimizer` (self) | any prior keyword mutation | ≤ 7d | overlapping campaign or ad group | soft-warn | Don't stack — let the prior change settle before another wave on the same scope |
| `/budget-optimizer` | budget raise / cut | ≤ 7d | overlapping campaign | soft-warn | Budget change still propagating; keyword pauses now compound the volume signal change |
| `/geo-schedule-optimizer` | geo / device / schedule modifier | ≤ 7d | overlapping campaign | soft-warn | Targeting moved; keyword performance is being re-baselined under new traffic mix |
| `/placement-optimizer` | placement exclusion (Display / PMax overlap) | ≤ 7d | overlapping campaign | soft-warn | Traffic mix moved (rare for Search-only optimizer scope; informational) |
| `/tracking-specialist` | conversion goal change | ≤ 30d | account-wide | hard-warn | Conversion baseline shifted — historical CPA/ROAS no longer comparable, so pause/tier decisions built on the audit's tier table need re-validation |
| any peer | manual UI change of keyword fields (status, match type, bid) | ≤ 14d | overlapping ad group | hard-warn | Treat operator UI edits as equivalent to a self mutation — don't overwrite an in-flight manual experiment |

### KW-E08-specific tightening

When operations include KW-E08 (bid-strategy target updates), **all bidding-related entries in the matrix above promote one verdict tier**:

- `/bidding-optimizer` target adjustment 2–7d → **hard-warn** (was soft-warn) — never stack two target moves on the same campaign inside the learning window.
- `/keyword-optimizer` self bid mutation ≤ 7d → **hard-warn** (was soft-warn) — same rationale.
- Any manual UI bid-field edit ≤ 14d → **hard-warn** (already hard-warn; reaffirm).

This stacks on top of the existing 5 KW-E08 rails (max-change, learning lockout, conversion floor, budget-cap joint constraint, portfolio linkage) — it does not replace them.

### Self-mutation lookup

Self-mutation windows already encoded for KW-E08 in `meta.learning_gate` are honored by `mutate.js`. Phase 0.4 reads the *same* `account-changelog.md` plus the optimizer's own `keyword-changelog.md` and additionally cross-references peer-skill mutations the existing learning gate doesn't see.

### Override

Hard-warns can be confirmed inline at the dry-run step (single-line "confirm" with the campaign/ad-group + window referenced explicitly). There is no flag to silence them ahead of time — every session re-prompts on the relevant scope. Hard-block (M/B dirty) cannot be confirmed inline; only fixing the upstream report unblocks.

---

## Output Contract for Phase 0.4

Phase 0.4 produces an in-memory object consumed by Phase 1 (operations generation) and Phase 2 (dry-run rendering):

```json
{
  "hard_blocks": [
    { "peer": "/tracking-specialist", "report": "context/analysis/tracking-audit.md", "date": "...", "finding": "..." }
  ],
  "hard_warns": [
    { "campaign_id": "...", "campaign": "...", "ad_group_id": "...", "ad_group": "...", "peer": "/account-changelog", "mutation": "ad-group restructure", "date": "...", "days_ago": 9, "window": 14 }
  ],
  "soft_warns": [
    { "campaign_id": "...", "campaign": "...", "ad_group": "...", "peer": "/quality-score-auditor", "score": 62, "finding": "AG-level QS 4 on swap-target ad group", "date": "..." }
  ],
  "informational": [ ... ],
  "freshness_notes": [
    "no fresh /lp-auditor",
    "/tracking-specialist mtime 5d older than header — surfaced as suspicious"
  ]
}
```

Routing:

- `hard_blocks` non-empty → Phase 1 does not run; Phase 2 prints the block reasons + handoff commands.
- `hard_warns` non-empty → Phase 2 prints them in the dry-run "Cross-skill context" with `WARN:` prefix and collects an explicit "confirm" line per affected scope before allowing Phase 3 (live apply).
- `soft_warns` and `informational` → surfaced in the dry-run "Cross-skill context" block above the mutation table, no gating.
- `freshness_notes` → printed at the bottom of "Cross-skill context" so the operator knows where the picture is incomplete.

---

## Sequencing reminder

The optimizer does **not** write a sequenced report (that's the auditor's job). The handoff matrix here exists only to:

1. Pre-flight gate the mutation (hard-block / hard-warn / soft-warn).
2. Enrich the dry-run output with quoted peer findings on the campaigns/ad groups being mutated.

The user already chose to run the optimizer. The Cross-skill context section's role is to give them the data to *halt or downscope* the plan before live apply — not to re-route them to other skills.

# PPCOS — Google Ads Workspace

You are a senior Google Ads strategist working alongside the user. Think in business outcomes, not just metrics. Be a thinking partner — have opinions, challenge assumptions, and lead with data. The user is a Google Ads specialist, not a developer. Talk to them as a peer strategist.

All business decisions, performance data, and analysis live as version-controlled files in `context/`. This is your shared workspace.

## Before Any Task

Read `context/business.md` first. Know the targets, constraints, and priorities before doing anything.
Read `context/account-changelog.md` for recent changes. If the "Last updated" timestamp is older than 5 days, tell the user to refresh it with `/account-changelog`.


Extract and hold:
- Primary KPI and mode (growth / balanced / cost control)
- Target CPA, ROAS, and hard constraints
- Campaign priorities (analyze these first)
- Competitive strategy and approach
- Known constraints (what can't be changed)

If `business.md` is missing critical data or it's not enough to make decisions, tell the user what's missing and why it matters before proceeding.

## How You Think

- Always tie recommendations back to business.md targets — never analyze in a vacuum
- Metrics override intent — a profitable search term stays, even if intent seems off
- Before recommending anything, check: do I have the data? If not, tell the user what to pull and which `/command` to run
- Flag stale data (>7 days for fast-moving metrics like CPA, conversions) before basing decisions on it
- Never guess at performance numbers — use actual data or say "I don't have this data yet"
- Connect dots across campaigns — if one campaign's insight applies elsewhere, say so
- After completing analysis or a task, suggest the next logical step
- Check `context/account-changelog.md` for recent budget changes before recommending budget or CPA/ROAS changes. If budget changed in the last 7 days, tell the user what changed and when

## When to Challenge the User

Don't just agree. If something doesn't add up, say so.

- Want to increase budget but CPA is above target? Push back with the numbers
- Want to pause something that's converting? Ask why, show the data
- Proposing a change that contradicts business.md constraints? Flag it explicitly
- Missing context that would change the decision? Say so before proceeding
- About to repeat something that failed before (check business.md "Historical Failures")? Warn them

Frame challenges as: "[what you want to do] vs [what the data shows] — here's what I'd suggest instead"

## How You Communicate

- Lead with impact: "$2,400/month saved" not "I recommend adjusting the bid strategy"
- Use numbers, not adjectives: "$45 CPA vs $200 target" not "CPA is quite high"
- Don't explain Google Ads concepts unless the user asks
- Short and direct — bullets over paragraphs
- When presenting options, give your recommendation and why
- When you spot a risk or opportunity while doing something else, flag it — don't stay silent

## Data & Context

All context lives in `context/`. Google Ads data in `context/google-ads/data/`, competitor ads in `context/competitor-ads/`, analysis reports in `context/analysis/`. Full file reference table: `.claude/rules/context-files.md`.

If data isn't available use the query.js to get the data using the API and put it into the correct place inside the `context/`.

Operational work logs go in `context/memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — see `.claude/rules/memory-logging.md` for when and how to log. If user mentions previous work also check the memory.

All outputs go to `created/` (importable files) or `context/analysis/` (reports). Output from subagents MUST go to `context/analysis/`.

## Security

- **NEVER read `config/.env`** — scripts load credentials automatically
- If credentials are missing, tell the user to configure `.env` (don't attempt to read or validate it)
- Never log, display, or include credential values in any output

## Report Generation

When users run a skill that generates a report into `context/analysis/`, offer to run the `/report-generator` hub-level skill.

# Landing Page Builder Skill

Generate a self-contained HTML landing page wireframe with real persuasive copy, brand-matched colors, and visual placeholders — ready to open in a browser and present to a client.

Built on the **Conversion Amplifier Framework** (Offer → Hierarchy → Copy → Design → Build).

## Command Format

```
/landing-page-builder [--skip-discovery] [--from-audit]
```

**Examples:**
- `/landing-page-builder` — Full interactive mode with 7-question discovery
- `/landing-page-builder --skip-discovery` — Derive settings from existing context files
- `/landing-page-builder --from-audit` — Use prior audit/optimize data (skips "use audit data?" confirmation)

---

## Process

### Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Check required context files:

| File | Required | If Missing |
|------|----------|------------|
| `context/brand.md` | Yes | Prompt: "Run `/ads-context [URL]` first" |
| `context/offer-angles.md` | Yes | Prompt: "Run `/offer-maker angles` first" |

**Optional files (enhance output if present):**

| File | Used For |
|------|----------|
| `context/brand-colours/palette.md` | Brand colours and fonts (from `/ads-context`). If missing, defaults are used |
| `context/business.md` | Business goals, constraints, previous test learnings |
| `context/google-ads/data/keywords.csv` | Primary keywords for message match in headline |
| `context/google-ads/data/ads.csv` | Existing ad copy for message match reference |

**If required files are missing, stop and show:**

```markdown
## Prerequisites Missing

To build a landing page wireframe, the following context is required:

| File | Status | Action |
|------|--------|--------|

### Phase 0.5: Prior Audit Integration

Check if prior LP audit and optimization reports exist. If they do, leverage their findings to pre-populate discovery settings and seed copy generation — avoiding redundant analysis.

| `keywords.themes_per_ad_group` | **H1 (when LP serves a specific AG)** | If the LP is dedicated to one ad group, mirror that AG's keyword theme in H1 (message match). If the LP serves multiple AGs, choose the dominant theme. |
| `keywords.primary_match_keywords` | **Hero sub-headline, benefits H2s** | Naturally weave 2-3 of the primary keywords into sub-headline + benefit titles. Don't keyword-stuff. |
| `competitive.competitor_positioning` | **Hero angle selection, differentiation copy** | If competitors all lead with one angle (e.g., speed), do NOT lead with the same. Choose a contrasting angle from `offer.recommended_angles`. Add a "differentiation" line in benefits/objections section that names what we do differently (without naming competitors). |
| `competitive.differentiation_gaps` | **Hero sub-headline, benefits, FAQ** | If there's an angle no competitor owns and our offer supports it, claim it explicitly in sub-headline or as a top benefit. |
| `quality_score.lpe_findings` + `quality_score.target_ad_groups` | **H1 + sub-headline** | If LPE is the limiting QS component on the target AG, force tight ad-text-to-H1 message match. Pull the best-performing ad headline from `context/google-ads/data/ads.csv` for that AG and mirror its structure in H1. |
| `quality_score.ar_findings` | **H1 specificity** | If AR is below average, the H1 must be highly specific to the search intent — avoid generic "the best [category]" headlines. |
| `strategy.break_even_cvr` | **CVR framing in Summary phase only** | Surface the break-even CVR in the Summary as context for the wireframe's CVR target. Do NOT bake target CPA/ROAS numbers into the LP copy itself (the LP is target-agnostic). |
| `strategy.posture` | **CTA aggressiveness** | aggressive → action-driven CTA ("Get my audit now"); efficient → value-first CTA ("See your savings"); balanced → as awareness default. |
| `tracking.status = dirty` | **Summary phase warning only** | Add a "verify tracking before launch" note in the handoff. Does NOT change copy. |

# Awareness Stages & Page Hierarchy Reference

Agent-readable reference combining awareness-level strategy with the 7-section landing page hierarchy blueprint.

---

## The 5 Awareness Stages

| Stage | What they know | What they need | Temperature |
|-------|---------------|----------------|-------------|
| **Unaware** | Doesn't know the problem exists | Problem identification | Cold |
| **Problem Aware** | Knows the problem, not the solutions | Problem validation + consequence | Cold |
| **Solution Aware** | Knows solutions exist, evaluating options | Your unique approach | Warm |
| **Product Aware** | Knows your product, comparing to alternatives | Specific benefits + differentiation | Warm |
| **Most Aware** | Ready to buy, needs the right offer | Offer details + urgency | Hot |

---

## Traffic Source → Awareness Mapping

| Traffic Source | Typical Stage | LP Approach |
|---------------|--------------|-------------|
| **Brand Search** | Most Aware | Direct offer, short-form, streamlined CTA |
| **Competitor Search** | Product Aware | Differentiators, heavy proof, comparison |
| **Product/Service Search** | Solution Aware | Benefits, unique approach, heavy trust/proof |
| **Problem Search** | Problem Aware | Problem agitation, education, long-form |
| **Display/YouTube** | Unaware → Problem Aware | Problem identification, content-heavy |
| **Remarketing** | Product Aware → Most Aware | Value boosters, risk removal, urgency |

---

## Message Strategy by Stage

### Unaware
- **Focus:** Problem identification — make them aware something is wrong
- **Tone:** Informative, eye-opening
- **Lead angle:** Problem/Pain (educational framing)
- **CTA type:** "Learn more" / "Discover"

### Problem Aware
- **Focus:** Problem articulation — validate frustration, show consequences
- **Tone:** Empathetic, understanding
- **Lead angle:** Problem/Pain (validation framing)
- **CTA type:** "Discover solution" / "See how"

### Solution Aware
- **Focus:** Your unique approach — differentiate from other solutions
- **Tone:** Authoritative, differentiating
- **Lead angle:** USP / Value Proposition
- **CTA type:** "See how it works" / "Compare"

### Product Aware
- **Focus:** Specific benefits & features — why you beat alternatives
- **Tone:** Confident, specific
- **Lead angle:** USP + Social Proof
- **CTA type:** "Compare options" / "See features"

### Most Aware
- **Focus:** Offer details & urgency — give them the deal, remove friction
- **Tone:** Direct, urgent
- **Lead angle:** Value Proposition + Risk Removal + Urgency
- **CTA type:** "Get started now" / "Buy now" / "Start free trial"

---

## Angle Priority by Stage

| Angle | Unaware | Problem Aware | Solution Aware | Product Aware | Most Aware |
|-------|---------|--------------|----------------|--------------|------------|
| **Problem/Pain** | LEAD | LEAD | Include | Light | Skip |
| **Value Proposition** | Light | Include | LEAD | LEAD | LEAD |
| **USPs** | Skip | Light | Include | LEAD | LEAD |
| **Value Boosters** | Skip | Skip | Light | Include | LEAD |
| **Social Proof** | Skip | Light | Include | LEAD | Include |
| **Risk Removal** | Skip | Skip | Light | Include | LEAD |

**LEAD** = Primary emphasis, multiple placements | **Include** = Present | **Light** = Brief mention | **Skip** = Omit

---

## The 7-Section Hierarchy Blueprint

| # | Section | Visitor's Question | Goal | Position |
|---|---------|-------------------|------|----------|
| 1 | **Hero** | What exactly is being offered? | Capture attention, communicate core value, establish relevance | Above the fold |
| 2 | **Benefits** | How will this help me? | Show outcomes and transformation, connect to desires | First scroll |
| 3 | **Trust/Authority** | Why should I believe you? | Establish credibility through credentials, certifications, expertise | After benefits |
| 4 | **Social Proof** | What do others say about this? | Provide third-party validation through testimonials, case studies, stats | After trust |
| 5 | **Objection Handling** | What if it doesn't work? | Remove mental friction, address doubts, provide guarantees | Middle of page |
| 6 | **Urgency/Scarcity** | Why should I act now? | Create legitimate FOMO, time or supply pressure | Before final CTA |
| 7 | **Call to Action** | What should I do next? | Provide clear direction, reinforce value, trigger conversion | Repeated throughout + final |

**Psychological progression:** Trust before proof, proof before pressure. Establish credibility → validate with others → then create urgency. Pressure on an unconvinced visitor causes bounces, not conversions.

---

## Section Emphasis by Awareness Level

Use this table to determine Full/Heavy/Moderate/Light/Skip for each section based on the visitor's awareness stage.

| Section | Most Aware | Product Aware | Solution Aware | Problem Aware | Unaware |
|---------|-----------|--------------|----------------|--------------|---------|
| 1. Hero | Full (direct offer) | Full (differentiators) | Full (outcome-focused) | Full (problem-focused) | Full (problem intro) |
| 2. Benefits | Light | Moderate | Heavy | Heavy (educational) | Heavy (educational) |
| 3. Trust/Authority | Light | Moderate | Heavy | Heavy | Heavy |
| 4. Social Proof | Light | Heavy | Heavy | Moderate | Moderate |
| 5. Objection Handling | Minimal | Moderate | Heavy | Heavy | Light |
| 6. Urgency/Scarcity | Strong | Moderate | Moderate | Light | Skip |
| 7. CTA | Repeated (3+) | Repeated (4+) | Repeated (5+) | Repeated (5+) | Repeated (3+) |

---

## Page Length by Awareness

| Awareness | Page Length | Sections Included | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Most Aware** | Short-form | Hero + light proof + CTA | They know you, just need the deal |
| **Product Aware** | Medium | All 7, moderate depth | Need differentiation and proof |
| **Solution Aware** | Full-length | All 7, heavy depth | Need education on your approach |
| **Problem Aware** | Long-form | All 7, heavy on 1-3 | Need problem validation first |
| **Unaware** | Long-form | All 7, heavy education | Need to discover the problem exists |

---

## Copywriting Framework by Awareness

| Awareness Level | Best Framework | Structure | Why |
|----------------|---------------|-----------|-----|
| **Unaware** | AIDA | Attention → Interest → Desire → Action | Need to capture attention and build interest from zero |
| **Problem Aware** | PAS | Problem → Agitation → Solution | They know the problem, agitate it then present solution |
| **Solution Aware** | AIDA or BAB | Before → After → Bridge | Show transformation from current state to desired state |
| **Product Aware** | Hook-Story-Offer | Hook → Story → Offer | Narrative differentiation, why you vs competitors |
| **Most Aware** | Direct Offer | Offer → Proof → CTA | Skip the story, lead with the deal |

Frameworks are not rigid. Combine elements across frameworks (e.g., PAS opening with AIDA middle).

---

## Section Detail Reference

### Section 1: Hero
- **Required:** Primary headline (under 10 words), sub-headline (under 2 sentences), visual element, primary CTA
- **Optional:** Microcopy near CTA, secondary CTA, anchor navigation
- **Rule:** 80% of visitors decide to stay or leave based on the hero alone
- **Key mistakes:** Vague headlines, generic stock photos, no CTA above fold, feature-focused headlines, no message match

### Section 2: Benefits
- **Three angles:** Functional (time/cost/ease), Business (efficiency/resources), Personal (stress/confidence)
- **Display patterns:** Icon + headline + description grid, before/after comparison, numbered list, feature-benefit pairs
- **Rule:** Benefits focus on outcomes, not features. Use "So what?" technique until you reach the emotional benefit

### Section 3: Trust/Authority
- **Types:** Institutional (certifications, compliance badges) and Expertise (awards, credentials, results)
- **By vertical:** Regulated industries → institutional trust first. Services/consulting → expertise trust first
- **Rule:** Trust must be established before social proof is effective

### Section 4: Social Proof
- **Types:** Testimonials, case studies, statistical proof, expert endorsements, third-party validation
- **Testimonial formula:** Specific result + before state + after state + recommendation
- **Rule:** Real, verifiable, specific. Full names and photos. Match to visitor segment

### Section 5: Objection Handling
- **Techniques:** Guarantee statements, FAQ sections, value framing, process clarifications, targeted testimonials
- **Common objections:** Price, value, implementation, timing, trust, fit
- **Rule:** Address top 3 objections proactively before they become conversion barriers

### Section 6: Urgency/Scarcity
- **Urgency:** Limited time offers, deadline-driven events, progressive deadlines, time-sensitive bonuses
- **Scarcity:** Limited quantity, exclusive access, founding member pricing
- **Rule:** Only legitimate techniques. Fake scarcity destroys trust permanently. Place after value and trust

### Section 7: Call to Action
- **Principles:** Value-focused, specific, first-person, contrasting, repeated
- **Placement:** After hero, after benefits, after social proof, after objection handling, after urgency, final section
- **Microcopy patterns:** Risk removal, social proof, speed/ease, urgency, value reinforcement

# CTA Patterns Reference

Agent-readable reference with 5 CTA types, microcopy patterns, and placement strategy for landing pages across Lead Gen, SaaS, and Ecommerce verticals.

---

## CTA Fundamentals

### Four CTA Principles

| Principle | Do | Don't |
|-----------|-----|-------|
| **Value-focused** | Emphasize what they get | Describe what they do |
| **First-person** | "Get my free assessment" | "Get your free assessment" |
| **Specific** | Include what happens next | Use vague action words |
| **Contrasting** | Button visually pops | Button blends into page |

### Primary vs Secondary CTAs

| | Primary CTA | Secondary CTA |
|--|-------------|---------------|
| **Purpose** | Drive the main conversion action | Offer a lower-commitment alternative |
| **Prominence** | Largest, most contrasting button | Smaller, less prominent |
| **Commitment** | Higher (buy, sign up, book) | Lower (download, watch, learn more) |
| **Usage** | Always present, repeated throughout | Optional, max 1, must advance same goal |

---

## The 5 CTA Types

| Type | Purpose | Best For |
|------|---------|----------|
| 1. Value-first | Lead with what they receive | High-value offers, free trials, consultations |
| 2. Action-driven | Direct command with benefit | Ecommerce purchases, simple signups |
| 3. Risk-removal | Neutralize hesitation | High-ticket offers, skeptical audiences |
| 4. Urgency-based | Create time pressure | Promotions, limited offers, launch events |
| 5. Low-commitment | Reduce friction with easy first step | Cold traffic, complex solutions, long sales cycles |

# Headline Patterns Reference

Agent-readable reference with 6 headline types, formulas, and examples for landing page hero sections across Lead Gen, SaaS, and Ecommerce verticals.

---

## Headline Fundamentals

### The 5-Second Rule
A visitor must understand the core value proposition within 5 seconds. The headline carries 80% of that job.

| Length | Verdict |
|--------|---------|
| Under 10 words | Ideal: scannable, punchy, clear |
| 10-15 words | Acceptable if every word earns its place |
| Over 15 words | Too long: loses attention, dilutes impact |

### Headline + Sub-headline Pairing
- **Headline** = outcome or transformation (what they get)
- **Sub-headline** = mechanism or proof (how or why it works)
- Never repeat the same idea in both lines

---

## The 6 Headline Types

| Type | Purpose | Best For |
|------|---------|----------|
| 1. Outcome | Promise the end result | Most Aware, Product Aware |
| 2. Problem-agitation | Name and intensify the pain | Problem Aware |
| 3. How-to | Promise a method or process | Solution Aware |
| 4. Proof/statistic | Lead with credibility | Product Aware, skeptical audiences |
| 5. Question | Trigger self-identification | Problem Aware, Unaware |
| 6. Direct offer | State the deal | Most Aware, promotions |

### Headline Type by Awareness Level

| Awareness | Primary Type | Secondary Type |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| **Unaware** | Question | Problem-agitation |
| **Problem Aware** | Problem-agitation | Question |
| **Solution Aware** | How-to | Outcome |
| **Product Aware** | Proof/statistic | Outcome |
| **Most Aware** | Direct offer | Outcome |

---

## Type 1: Outcome Headlines

**Formula:** `[Desired outcome] + [specificity or timeframe]`

### Lead Gen
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Close 30% More Deals This Quarter" | "The sales acceleration system trusted by 200+ B2B teams" | Specific outcome (30%), time-bound (quarter), relevant metric |
| "Get Qualified Leads That Actually Convert" | "Stop wasting budget on leads your sales team ignores" | Addresses quality over quantity, real frustration |
| "Double Your Pipeline Without Doubling Your Budget" | "See how we help agencies scale lead gen profitably" | Growth promise with efficiency constraint |

### SaaS
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Cut Your Reporting Time by 80%" | "Automated dashboards that update while you sleep" | Specific number (80%), tangible benefit (time saved) |
| "Ship Features 3x Faster" | "The development workflow trusted by 500+ engineering teams" | Outcome-first, social proof in sub-headline |
| "Stop Losing Customers to Churn" | "Predict and prevent cancellations before they happen" | Names the enemy, promises prevention |

### Ecommerce
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Sleep Better Starting Tonight" | "Premium memory foam mattresses, 100-night risk-free trial" | Immediate outcome, risk removal in sub-headline |
| "Run Faster, Recover Sooner" | "Performance running shoes engineered for distance runners" | Dual outcome, specific audience segment |
| "Professional Results at Home" | "Salon-grade hair tools used by 50,000+ stylists" | Outcome + social proof |

---

## Type 2: Problem-Agitation Headlines

**Formula:** `[Pain point] + [consequence or amplification]`

### Lead Gen
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Tired of Leads That Ghost Your Sales Team?" | "The qualification system that filters out time-wasters before they reach your inbox" | Names specific frustration, promises mechanism |

| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |

| "Your Data Is Scattered Across 12 Tools" | "One dashboard. Every metric. Zero tab-switching" | Specific number, clear solution in sub-headline |

### Ecommerce
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|

| "Another Day, Another Bad Hair Day" | "The styling tool that works in 3 minutes flat" | Relatable daily frustration, specific time promise |

---

## Type 3: How-To Headlines

**Formula:** `How to [desired outcome] + [constraint or qualifier]`

### Lead Gen
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |

| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |

## Type 4: Proof/Statistic Headlines

**Formula:** `[Specific statistic or result] + [context]`

| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |

| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |

| "99.9% Uptime, Zero Excuses" | "Enterprise-grade reliability at startup-friendly pricing" | Technical proof, addresses two concerns |

### Ecommerce
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Rated 4.9/5 by 23,000 Customers" | "The skincare routine dermatologists recommend most" | Volume + expert endorsement |
| "50,000 Runners Can't Be Wrong" | "The shoe that won Runner's World Best in Class" | Social proof + authority endorsement |

---

## Type 5: Question Headlines

**Formula:** `[Question that the target audience answers "yes" to]`

### Lead Gen
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Ready to Stop Losing Deals to Faster Competitors?" | "Speed-to-lead automation that responds in under 60 seconds" | Yes/no self-selection, specific mechanism |
| "What If Every Lead Your Sales Team Called Was Pre-Qualified?" | "AI-powered lead scoring that filters before your team dials" | Hypothetical paints the ideal state |

### SaaS
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "What Would You Do With 15 Extra Hours Per Week?" | "Automate the reports. Focus on the strategy" | Quantifies benefit as free time |

### Ecommerce
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Still Waking Up With Back Pain?" | "Join 30,000 people who fixed their sleep with one mattress change" | Self-identification, social proof in sub-headline |

---

## Type 6: Direct Offer Headlines

**Formula:** `[Offer] + [key differentiator or urgency]`

### Lead Gen
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Free Google Ads Audit: Find Your Wasted Spend" | "15-minute analysis. Zero commitment. Actionable recommendations" | Clear offer, removes risk, sets expectations |
| "Get Your Custom Growth Plan in 24 Hours" | "Book a strategy call. We build your roadmap live" | Specific deliverable, fast turnaround |

### SaaS
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Start Free for 14 Days. No Credit Card Required" | "Full access to every feature. Cancel anytime" | Removes every barrier |
| "60% Off Annual Plans This Week Only" | "Lock in the lowest price we've ever offered" | Clear discount, time pressure |

### Ecommerce
| Headline | Sub-headline | Why It Works |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| "Buy 2, Get 1 Free" | "Our bestselling bundle, only available this weekend" | Simple math, clear value, urgency |
| "Free Shipping on Orders Over $50" | "Plus a 60-day return guarantee on everything" | Removes friction, adds risk reversal |

---

## Message Match Rule

The LP headline must mirror the ad copy that drove the click. Mismatched headlines cause immediate bounces.

| Ad Copy | Matching LP Headline | Mismatched LP Headline |
|---------|---------------------|----------------------|
| "Get a Free Google Ads Audit" | "Your Free Google Ads Audit Starts Here" | "Welcome to Our Marketing Agency" |
| "50% Off Running Shoes" | "50% Off: Premium Running Shoes" | "Shop Our Collection" |
| "Cut Your Reporting Time by 80%" | "Cut Reporting Time by 80% With Automated Dashboards" | "The #1 Analytics Platform" |

For Search traffic: headline should contain the primary keyword or close variant.

# HTML Template Reference

Agent-readable reference with CSS variable system, section HTML snippets, and responsive rules for generating self-contained landing page wireframes.

---

## HTML Structure

The generated file must be a single self-contained HTML file with:
- All CSS inline in a `<style>` block in the `<head>`
- No external CSS/JS dependencies
- No JavaScript (except optional smooth-scroll for anchor nav)
- Semantic HTML5 elements (`<section>`, `<header>`, `<main>`)

### Base Structure

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>{Company} — {Offer Type} Landing Page</title>
    <style>
        /* CSS Variables */
        :root {
            --color-primary: #1a1a2e;
            --color-secondary: #16213e;
            --color-accent: #e94560;
            --color-accent-hover: #d63851;
            --color-bg: #ffffff;
            --color-bg-alt: #f8f9fa;
            --color-text: #333333;
            --color-text-light: #666666;
            --color-text-on-accent: #ffffff;
            --color-border: #e0e0e0;
            --font-heading: 'system-ui', -apple-system, sans-serif;
            --font-body: 'system-ui', -apple-system, sans-serif;
            --container-max: 1100px;
            --section-padding: 80px 20px;
            --section-padding-mobile: 48px 16px;
            --border-radius: 8px;
            --cta-padding: 16px 32px;
            --cta-padding-mobile: 16px 24px;
            --cta-font-size: 18px;
        }

        /* Reset & Base */
        *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
        html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }
        body {
            font-family: var(--font-body);
            color: var(--color-text);
            background: var(--color-bg);
            line-height: 1.6;
            -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
        }

        /* Container */
        .container {
            max-width: var(--container-max);
            margin: 0 auto;
            padding: 0 20px;
        }

        /* Section Base */
        section { padding: var(--section-padding); }
        section:nth-child(even) { background: var(--color-bg-alt); }

        /* Typography */
        h1 { font-family: var(--font-heading); font-size: 2.8rem; line-height: 1.15; font-weight: 800; color: var(--color-primary); }
        h2 { font-family: var(--font-heading); font-size: 2rem; line-height: 1.25; font-weight: 700; color: var(--color-primary); margin-bottom: 16px; }
        h3 { font-family: var(--font-heading); font-size: 1.25rem; line-height: 1.35; font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-primary); margin-bottom: 8px; }
        p { margin-bottom: 16px; color: var(--color-text); }
        .text-light { color: var(--color-text-light); }
        .text-center { text-align: center; }

        /* CTA Button */
        .cta-button {
            display: inline-block;
            background: var(--color-accent);
            color: var(--color-text-on-accent);
            padding: var(--cta-padding);
            font-size: var(--cta-font-size);
            font-weight: 700;
            text-decoration: none;
            border-radius: var(--border-radius);
            border: none;
            cursor: pointer;
            transition: background 0.2s ease;
        }
        .cta-button:hover { background: var(--color-accent-hover); }
        .cta-microcopy {
            display: block;
            font-size: 0.85rem;
            color: var(--color-text-light);
            margin-top: 8px;
        }

        /* Visual Placeholder */
        .placeholder {
            border: 2px dashed var(--color-border);
            border-radius: var(--border-radius);
            padding: 40px 20px;
            text-align: center;
            color: var(--color-text-light);
            font-style: italic;
            background: var(--color-bg-alt);
            margin: 24px 0;
        }

        /* Grid Layouts */
        .grid-2 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 32px; align-items: center; }
        .grid-3 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr; gap: 24px; }
        .grid-4 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; gap: 20px; }

        /* Cards */
        .card {
            background: var(--color-bg);
            border: 1px solid var(--color-border);
            border-radius: var(--border-radius);
            padding: 24px;
        }

        /* Testimonial */
        .testimonial {
            background: var(--color-bg);
            border-left: 4px solid var(--color-accent);
            padding: 24px;
            border-radius: 0 var(--border-radius) var(--border-radius) 0;
            margin-bottom: 24px;
        }
        .testimonial-text { font-style: italic; font-size: 1.05rem; margin-bottom: 12px; }
        .testimonial-author { font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-primary); }
        .testimonial-role { font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--color-text-light); }

        /* FAQ */
        .faq-item { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-border); padding: 20px 0; }
        .faq-question { font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-primary); margin-bottom: 8px; font-size: 1.1rem; }
        .faq-answer { color: var(--color-text); }

        /* Trust Badges */
        .trust-bar {
            display: flex;
            justify-content: center;
            align-items: center;
            gap: 40px;
            flex-wrap: wrap;
            padding: 20px 0;
        }
        .trust-item { text-align: center; color: var(--color-text-light); font-size: 0.9rem; }

        /* Urgency Banner */
        .urgency-banner {
            background: var(--color-primary);
            color: var(--color-text-on-accent);
            text-align: center;
            padding: 16px 20px;
            font-weight: 600;
        }

        /* Responsive: Mobile First */
        @media (max-width: 768px) {
            section { padding: var(--section-padding-mobile); }
            h1 { font-size: 1.9rem; }
            h2 { font-size: 1.5rem; }
            .grid-2, .grid-3, .grid-4 { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
            .cta-button {
                display: block;
                width: 100%;
                text-align: center;
                padding: var(--cta-padding-mobile);
            }
            .trust-bar { gap: 20px; }
        }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Sections go here -->
</body>
</html>
```

---

# Quality Checklist Reference

Agent-readable checklist for validating generated landing page wireframes. Adapted from the LP Quality Checklist for wireframe context (skips PageSpeed, tracking, live-only checks; focuses on layout, copy, CTA, and structure).

---

## When to Use

Run this checklist after generating the HTML wireframe in Phase 6 of the Landing Page Builder skill. Check the generated file against all applicable categories below.

---

## 1. Offer Completeness

- [ ] Core value proposition is stated in one clear sentence
- [ ] Unique selling points are explicitly stated on the page
- [ ] Value boosters are present (bonuses, extras, bundles)
- [ ] Social proof is present (or placeholder marked)
- [ ] Risk removal element exists (guarantee, free trial, return policy)
- [ ] All five Irresistible Offer components are represented

---

## 2. Hero Section

- [ ] Primary headline is under 10 words
- [ ] Headline communicates the core outcome, not a feature
- [ ] Sub-headline adds specificity without repeating the headline
- [ ] A stranger can understand the value proposition within 5 seconds
- [ ] Visual placeholder is present and descriptive (e.g., "[Product Screenshot]")
- [ ] Primary CTA is visible in the hero section
- [ ] CTA button text is benefit-driven and first-person
- [ ] CTA button has contrasting color against the background

---

## 3. Benefits Section

- [ ] Benefits focus on outcomes, not features
- [ ] At least two of three angles covered (functional, business, personal)
- [ ] "So what?" test passed: each benefit answers why the visitor should care
- [ ] No jargon: a non-expert can understand every benefit

---

## 4. Trust/Authority Section

- [ ] At least one trust element is present (or placeholder marked)
- [ ] Trust claims are specific and verifiable, not vague
- [ ] Trust type matches the vertical (institutional for regulated, expertise for services)
- [ ] Trust section appears before social proof section in page order

---

## 5. Social Proof Section

- [ ] At least one form of social proof is present (or placeholder marked)
- [ ] Testimonial placeholders include guidance: "[Replace with: full name, photo, company, specific result]"
- [ ] Social proof is specific with results, not generic
- [ ] Proof matches the target visitor segment

---

## 6. Objection Handling

- [ ] Top 3 visitor objections are identified and addressed
- [ ] FAQ section covers key concerns (pricing, implementation, timing, trust)
- [ ] Guarantee is specific (duration, process, conditions)
- [ ] Guarantee is placed near a conversion point

---

## 7. Urgency/Scarcity (if included)

- [ ] Urgency or scarcity is legitimate (placeholders note "replace with real deadline")
- [ ] Specific numbers and dates are used (not "limited time" or "act now")
- [ ] Reason for limitation is explained or placeholder provided
- [ ] Urgency appears after value and trust are established (correct page position)

---

## 8. Call to Action

- [ ] Primary CTA is repeated at least 3 times throughout the page
- [ ] CTA placement follows hierarchy: hero, after proof, after objections, final section
- [ ] CTA button text is consistent across placements (same action, same language)
- [ ] Microcopy near CTA reinforces the decision (risk removal, social proof, or urgency)
- [ ] Secondary CTA (if used) is clearly subordinate to primary

---

## 9. Copy Quality

- [ ] Active voice throughout ("Get your assessment" not "An assessment can be requested")
- [ ] No hedging language ("Do X" not "You might want to consider X")
- [ ] Visitor-first language (focuses on their reality, not your company)
- [ ] Specific numbers and results where possible
- [ ] No jargon or corporate speak

---

## 10. One-Page-One-Goal Rule

- [ ] No navigation bar (or only anchor links to same-page sections)
- [ ] No footer links (except legal placeholder if needed)
- [ ] No social media icons
- [ ] No competing offers or CTAs that lead away from primary goal
- [ ] Every element either drives conversion or is a placeholder with clear purpose

---

## 11. Visual & Layout (Wireframe-Specific)

- [ ] Sections follow the 7-section hierarchy order
- [ ] Each section has visual separation (alternating backgrounds or spacing)
- [ ] CTA buttons are visually distinct (contrasting color, sufficient size)
- [ ] Image placeholders are descriptive with "[Replace with...]" instructions
- [ ] Layout is responsive: single column below 768px
- [ ] CTAs go full-width on mobile viewport
- [ ] Sufficient white space between sections
- [ ] Brand colors are applied via CSS variables (`:root` block present)
- [ ] Font family matches brand (or sensible fallback)

---

## 12. Brand & Message Match

- [ ] Brand colors are correctly applied (primary, secondary, accent/CTA)
- [ ] Tone matches brand voice from `context/brand.md`
- [ ] Copy uses phrases from `context/offer-angles.md` where appropriate
- [ ] If keywords available: headline contains primary keyword or close variant
- [ ] Offer on page matches what would be promised in ads

## Scoring

Count passing items across all applicable categories:

| Score | Rating | Action |
|-------|--------|--------|
| 90-100% | Excellent | Ready for client review |
| 75-89% | Good | Minor fixes needed before sharing |
| 60-74% | Fair | Address failing items before client review |
| Below 60% | Needs Work | Significant revision required |

2. ...

# Section Content Patterns Reference

Agent-readable reference with content patterns for all 7 landing page sections, organized by vertical (Lead Gen, SaaS, Ecommerce).

---

## Section 1: Hero Patterns

### Required Elements

| Element | Purpose | Constraint |
|---------|---------|-----------|
| Primary headline | Core value proposition | Under 10 words, outcome-focused |
| Sub-headline | Expand with specifics | Under 2 sentences, don't repeat headline |
| Visual element | Reinforce the message | Product shot, demo video, or transformation image |
| Primary CTA | Tell visitor what to do | Benefit-driven text, contrasting color |

### Hero by Vertical

| Vertical | Visual Approach | Headline Focus | Sub-headline Focus |
|----------|----------------|---------------|-------------------|
| **Lead Gen** | Client results dashboard, team photo, process diagram | Outcome the service delivers | Mechanism or social proof |
| **SaaS** | Product screenshot, demo GIF, interface preview | Time/cost saved or capability unlocked | Free trial offer or social proof |
| **Ecommerce** | Hero product shot (lifestyle context), video | Product benefit or transformation | Risk removal (returns, shipping, warranty) |

### Hero Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| "Welcome to Our Platform" | Lead with the outcome or transformation |
| Generic stock photo | Use real product shots, team photos, or results |
| No CTA above the fold | Primary CTA must be visible without scrolling |
| Feature-focused headline | Translate every feature into a benefit |
| No message match with ad | Mirror ad headline language in LP headline |

---

## Section 2: Benefits Patterns

### Three Benefit Angles

| Angle | Focus | Lead Gen | SaaS | Ecommerce |
|-------|-------|----------|------|-----------|
| **Functional** | Time, cost, ease, results | "Save 5 hours per week on reporting" | "Deploy in 3 clicks, not 3 sprints" | "Charges in 30 minutes, lasts all day" |
| **Business** | Efficiency, resources, compliance | "Reduce acquisition costs by 30%" | "One tool replaces your 5-tool stack" | "Free shipping on all orders, every time" |
| **Personal** | Stress, confidence, recognition | "Stop worrying about pipeline at 2am" | "Look like a data genius in your next meeting" | "Compliments guaranteed or your money back" |

### Benefits Display Patterns

| Pattern | When to Use | Structure |
|---------|------------|-----------|
| **Icon + headline + description** | 3-6 benefits, visual scanning | Grid of benefit cards |
| **Before/after comparison** | Transformation-focused offers | Two-column table or visual |
| **Numbered list** | Process or methodology benefits | Sequential numbered items |
| **Feature-benefit pairs** | Technical products that need translation | Two-column: feature on left, benefit on right |

### FAB (Feature → Advantage → Benefit) Examples

| Feature | Advantage | Benefit (use on page) |
|---------|-----------|----------------------|
| 24/7 support chat | Get help anytime | "Never be stuck with an issue, even at midnight" |
| AI-powered analytics | Automatic insights | "Know exactly where to optimize without manual analysis" |
| 100-night trial | Try before you commit | "Sleep on it for 100 nights. If you don't love it, we take it back" |

---

## Section 3: Trust/Authority Patterns

### Trust Elements by Type

| Type | Examples | Best For |
|------|---------|----------|
| **Institutional** | ISO certifications, SOC 2, GDPR badges, SSL, industry associations | Finance, healthcare, legal, B2B enterprise |
| **Expertise** | Awards, media mentions ("As seen in"), credentials, years in business, results | Services, consulting, marketing, tech |
| **Scale** | Customer count, revenue processed, data points analyzed | SaaS, enterprise, high-volume ecommerce |

### Trust by Vertical

| Vertical | Primary Trust Approach | Examples |
|----------|----------------------|---------|
| **Lead Gen** | Expertise + results | "43% average ROI increase in 90 days," "Google Premier Partner," "15 years in PPC" |
| **SaaS** | Scale + security | "Trusted by 10,000+ teams," "SOC 2 Type 2 certified," "99.9% uptime SLA" |
| **Ecommerce** | Quality + safety | "Dermatologist tested," "Organic certified," "Made in the EU," "100,000+ orders shipped" |

### Trust Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| "We can be trusted" (vague) | "SOC 2 Type 2 certified, audited annually" (specific) |
| Fake or obscure awards | Use real, recognizable credentials only |
| Unverifiable claims | Link to supporting data or third-party source |
| Too many logos without context | Select 3-5 most recognizable, add "trusted by X companies" |

---

## Section 4: Social Proof Patterns

### Five Social Proof Types

| Type | Pattern | When to Use |
|------|---------|------------|
| **Testimonials** | Quote + name + photo + company | Always: place near relevant objections |
| **Case studies** | Before/after + specific metrics | Complex solutions, high-ticket, B2B |
| **Statistical proof** | "Used by 50,000 businesses" / "99.9% uptime" | SaaS, services, products with volume |
| **Expert endorsements** | Authority quote + credentials | When recognizable experts exist |
| **Third-party validation** | G2, Capterra, Trustpilot ratings + badge | SaaS, services, products with external reviews |

### Testimonial Formula

```
[Specific result] + [before state] + [after state] + [recommendation]
```

| Vertical | Weak | Strong |
|----------|------|--------|
| **Lead Gen** | "Great agency, highly recommend!" | "Pipeline went from $1.2M to $3.8M in 6 months. Before working with them, we couldn't scale past $50K/month in spend." — Sarah K., VP Marketing, TechCorp |
| **SaaS** | "Love this product!" | "Cut our reporting time from 15 hours to 45 minutes per week. Our team actually looks forward to Monday standup now." — Mike D., Head of Growth, ScaleUp Inc |
| **Ecommerce** | "Nice mattress" | "After 3 months, my back pain is gone. I've tried 4 other mattresses. This is the first one I didn't return." — James L., verified buyer |

### "Ugly Proof" Patterns (Scroll-Stoppers)

| Pattern | Example | Why It Works |
|---------|---------|--------------|
| Screenshot of real chat | Slack message: "These numbers are insane" | Feels genuine, not manufactured |
| Raw dashboard screenshot | Google Ads screenshot showing 5x ROAS | Data is hard to fake, instantly credible |
| Video testimonial thumbnail | Unscripted customer on camera | Video is harder to fake than text |
| Social media post embed | Twitter/LinkedIn post praising the product | Public post is verifiable |

---

## Section 5: Objection Handling Patterns

### Techniques

| Technique | Pattern | Example |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| **Guarantee** | "[Duration] guarantee + [simple process]" | "60-day money-back guarantee. Email us, get a refund within 48 hours. No questions, no hassle." |
| **FAQ section** | "Q: [Common concern] A: [Direct answer]" | Address top 5-7 concerns in expandable Q&A format |
| **Value framing** | Compare cost to alternatives or inaction | "At $299/month, that's less than $10/day — cheaper than the intern you'd need to do this manually" |
| **Process clarification** | Step-by-step with time estimates | "Step 1: Upload photos (5 min). Step 2: AI processes (2 hrs). Step 3: Download (5 min)." |
| **Targeted testimonial** | Objection-specific proof near the concern | Testimonial about easy implementation next to "How it works" section |

### Top Objections by Vertical

| Vertical | Top Objections | Handling Patterns |
|----------|---------------|------------------|
| **Lead Gen** | "Is this worth the retainer?" "How long until results?" "What if it doesn't work?" | ROI calculator, timeline with milestones, performance guarantee |
| **SaaS** | "Is it hard to set up?" "What about my existing tools?" "What if my team doesn't adopt it?" | Setup time promise, integration list, adoption stats/onboarding support |
| **Ecommerce** | "Is the quality good?" "What if it doesn't fit?" "Is shipping fast?" | Review highlights, return policy, shipping timeline |

---

## Section 6: Urgency/Scarcity Patterns

### Urgency Patterns

| Pattern | Structure | Example |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| **Limited time offer** | "[Discount] for the next [timeframe]" | "60% off for the next 37 hours" |
| **Progressive deadline** | Price increases over time | "Early bird: €200. After May 15: €249. After May 25: €299" |
| **Time-sensitive bonus** | Extra value that expires | "First 25 buyers get a 1-on-1 coaching call" |
| **Deadline-driven event** | Tied to external date | "Masterclass starts June 10th. Registration closes Friday" |

### Scarcity Patterns

| Pattern | Structure | Example |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| **Limited quantity** | "[Number] remaining" | "Only 8 spots left in the June cohort" |
| **Exclusive access** | Waitlist or application | "We onboard 5 new clients per month" |
| **Founding member pricing** | Locked rate for early adopters | "Founding member pricing locked for life" |

### Rules for Legitimate Urgency

- Explain why the limitation exists (builds credibility)
- Use specific numbers and dates, not "expires soon"
- Never fake scarcity — countdown timers that reset destroy trust permanently
- Place after value and trust are established

---

## Section 7: Final CTA Patterns

### Final Section Structure

| Element | Purpose | Example |
|---------|---------|---------|
| **Value recap headline** | Summarize the full offer | "Everything You Need to Scale Your Pipeline" |
| **Bullet summary** | 3-5 key value points | Key benefits, what's included, guarantee |
| **Primary CTA** | Largest, most prominent on the page | "Get My Free Growth Plan" |
| **Risk-removal microcopy** | Final reassurance | "No credit card. No commitment. Just results." |
| **Urgency reminder** | Last push if applicable | "Only 3 spots left this month" |

### Final CTA by Vertical

| Vertical | Recap Focus | CTA Emphasis |
|----------|-----------|--------------|
| **Lead Gen** | What they get + what happens next | "Book My Strategy Call — here's what we'll cover in 30 minutes" |
| **SaaS** | Full feature access + risk removal | "Start My Free Trial — full access, no credit card, cancel anytime" |
| **Ecommerce** | Product value + guarantee + urgency | "Order Now — free shipping, 60-day returns, ships today" |

```

# PPCOS — Google Ads Workspace

You are a senior Google Ads strategist working alongside the user. Think in business outcomes, not just metrics. Be a thinking partner — have opinions, challenge assumptions, and lead with data. The user is a Google Ads specialist, not a developer. Talk to them as a peer strategist.

All business decisions, performance data, and analysis live as version-controlled files in `context/`. This is your shared workspace.

## Before Any Task

Read `context/business.md` first. Know the targets, constraints, and priorities before doing anything.
Read `context/account-changelog.md` for recent changes. If the "Last updated" timestamp is older than 5 days, tell the user to refresh it with `/account-changelog`.


Extract and hold:
- Primary KPI and mode (growth / balanced / cost control)
- Target CPA, ROAS, and hard constraints
- Campaign priorities (analyze these first)
- Competitive strategy and approach
- Known constraints (what can't be changed)

If `business.md` is missing critical data or it's not enough to make decisions, tell the user what's missing and why it matters before proceeding.

## How You Think

- Always tie recommendations back to business.md targets — never analyze in a vacuum
- Metrics override intent — a profitable search term stays, even if intent seems off
- Before recommending anything, check: do I have the data? If not, tell the user what to pull and which `/command` to run
- Flag stale data (>7 days for fast-moving metrics like CPA, conversions) before basing decisions on it
- Never guess at performance numbers — use actual data or say "I don't have this data yet"
- Connect dots across campaigns — if one campaign's insight applies elsewhere, say so
- After completing analysis or a task, suggest the next logical step
- Check `context/account-changelog.md` for recent budget changes before recommending budget or CPA/ROAS changes. If budget changed in the last 7 days, tell the user what changed and when

## When to Challenge the User

Don't just agree. If something doesn't add up, say so.

- Want to increase budget but CPA is above target? Push back with the numbers
- Want to pause something that's converting? Ask why, show the data
- Proposing a change that contradicts business.md constraints? Flag it explicitly
- Missing context that would change the decision? Say so before proceeding
- About to repeat something that failed before (check business.md "Historical Failures")? Warn them

Frame challenges as: "[what you want to do] vs [what the data shows] — here's what I'd suggest instead"

## How You Communicate

- Lead with impact: "$2,400/month saved" not "I recommend adjusting the bid strategy"
- Use numbers, not adjectives: "$45 CPA vs $200 target" not "CPA is quite high"
- Don't explain Google Ads concepts unless the user asks
- Short and direct — bullets over paragraphs
- When presenting options, give your recommendation and why
- When you spot a risk or opportunity while doing something else, flag it — don't stay silent

## Data & Context

All context lives in `context/`. Google Ads data in `context/google-ads/data/`, competitor ads in `context/competitor-ads/`, analysis reports in `context/analysis/`. Full file reference table: `.claude/rules/context-files.md`.

If data isn't available use the query.js to get the data using the API and put it into the correct place inside the `context/`.

Operational work logs go in `context/memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — see `.claude/rules/memory-logging.md` for when and how to log. If user mentions previous work also check the memory.

All outputs go to `created/` (importable files) or `context/analysis/` (reports). Output from subagents MUST go to `context/analysis/`.

## Security

- **NEVER read `config/.env`** — scripts load credentials automatically
- If credentials are missing, tell the user to configure `.env` (don't attempt to read or validate it)
- Never log, display, or include credential values in any output

## Report Generation

When users run a skill that generates a report into `context/analysis/`, offer to run the `/report-generator` hub-level skill.

# LP Auditor Skill

Audits landing page quality across 6 modules (40 diagnostics). DIAGNOSE-ONLY — findings route to lp-optimizer, landing-page-builder, or ecom-page-builder for execution.

| Module | IDs | Checks |
|--------|-----|--------|
| **Structural** | D01-D12 | Offer completeness, hero clarity, CTA quality, benefits, trust, social proof, objections, guarantee, section hierarchy |
| **Message Match** | D13-D16 | Ad-to-LP headline match, offer match, keyword relevance, visual consistency |
| **Technical** | D17-D24 | Page speed, Core Web Vitals, mobile responsiveness, mobile CVR gap, forms, SSL, images |
| **Performance** | D25-D31 | CVR vs benchmark, per-LP CPA, device splits, traffic source match |
| **URL Health** | D32-D37 | HTTP status codes, redirect chains, DSA URLs, keyword URLs, asset URLs, URL expansion |
| **Ecommerce** | D38-D40 | Product page elements, cart/checkout flow, category page quality |

**Not checked by this skill (per de-duplication log):**
- Conversion tracking setup → tracking-specialist
- Ad copy quality → ad-copy-specialist
- Offer quality → offer-auditor
- Account structure → account-auditor

## Command Format

```
/lp-auditor                          # Default: entry gate selector (choose module or full)
/lp-auditor structural               # D01-D12 only
/lp-auditor message-match            # D13-D16 only
/lp-auditor technical                # D17-D24 only
/lp-auditor performance              # D25-D31 only
/lp-auditor urls                     # D32-D37 only
/lp-auditor ecommerce                # D38-D40 only
```

All subcommands accept an optional `--url=https://...` flag to pre-load a target URL.

**Examples:**
- `/lp-auditor` — Interactive selector, then full or module-specific audit
- `/lp-auditor structural --url=https://example.com` — Structural audit of specific URL
- `/lp-auditor urls` — Batch URL health check across all active final URLs
- `/lp-auditor performance` — Per-LP performance analysis from Google Ads data

## Data Sources

| File | Required | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| `context/business.md` | Recommended | Vertical detection (lead gen / SaaS / ecommerce) |
| `context/google-ads/data/ads.csv` | Yes (message-match, urls, performance) | Ad headlines, descriptions, final URLs |
| `context/google-ads/data/keywords.csv` | Yes (message-match) | Keywords mapped to ad groups |
